A Day in the Life: On a cross-functional team, your day is spent turning fuzzy needs into a clear, agreed picture of what to build. You carry out the core requirements work: running intake and kickoff conversations, gathering and refining requirements, writing user stories and acceptance criteria, and framing the problems worth solving. You are also accountable for what those requirements become, making sure they flow cleanly into wireframes, prototypes, customer experience maps, and SEO, so what gets built matches what was agreed. Beyond that, you are consulted across nearly the whole team, from research and design to development and go-to-market, since almost every decision touches what to build and why. A typical day mixes focused writing, drafting stories and acceptance criteria in Notion and Trello, with a lot of conversation: a standup, a refinement session, and working time with designers, engineers, and stakeholders to keep everyone aligned. You work in short loops, share drafts early, and adjust as the team learns.
